title: DeepSeek
summary: Chinese lab whose open-weight reasoning models reset assumptions about training cost.
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

DeepSeek released open-weight models in late 2024 and a reasoning model in January 2025 that matched leading US systems on several benchmarks at a fraction of the reported training spend. Its published V3 figures describe roughly 2.8 million H800 GPU-hours, about US$5.6m of compute at market rates. The models are downloadable, which makes the cost curve a competitive fact rather than a vendor claim.

Technology Exposure

  • Open-weight reasoning and coding models.
  • Cost-efficient training and inference recipes.

What To Watch

  • Whether reported training costs include the full research programme.
  • Sustained model quality without access to the newest accelerators.

Record Notes

Editorial brief compiled 18 November 2026 from company disclosures, agency publications and press reporting. Figures are as reported by those sources and have not been independently audited; no live market data is used.

businessMeaning: Open weights plus low reported cost mean the model layer is unlikely to stay a durable toll booth.
investmentLens: The investable question is who captures the surplus when model capability is cheap: hardware, distribution, or proprietary data.
